You don’t see it, but it’s there. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics – from saving emissions in the City of Lights to powering the Mars Rover to protecting the F-35 fighter jet. Develop, communicate and drive a proactive Supplier Quality program for the business
Measure, maintain, analyze and communicate all Supplier Quality metrics, risks, and planned actions, and drive continuous improvements efforts at suppliers for improvement (CAR meetings, SRB, Mitigation meetings, etc.)

Strong and demonstrated communication skills (written, verbal, visual) and interpersonal skills (listening and communicating within group working environment).
Organizational skills – can marshal resources to get things done, orchestrate multiple activities at once to accomplish a goal, use matrixed resources effectively and efficiently, and arrange information in a useful manner.

Engineering or Technical Bachelor's Degree
Master’s degree
Strong knowledge of AS9100/AS9102/AS9145
Supply Chain management experience

As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.

Reporting to the Vice President, Operational Excellence & Transformation, the Director leads a portfolio of priority initiatives and manages the day-to-day delivery of the Operational Excellence Office. The role concentrates on Operations—manufacturing, supply chain, planning, procurement, quality, logistics, and field operations—and leads cross-functional work involving Finance, Engineering, Sales, IT, HR, and other functions when processes span organizational boundaries. The Director turns strategic priorities into executable programs, builds Lean and Kaizen capability, partners on systems and automation, and delivers measurable improvements in customer experience, productivity, operating margin, working capital, and cash flow.
Key Responsibilities
Program Portfolio and Governance
Translate VP priorities into initiative charters, integrated plans, milestones, resource needs, risks, and decisions.
Manage portfolio reviews, stage gates, executive reporting, and escalation processes; recommend sequencing based on value, capacity, and execution risk.
Lead program managers as we build up the team, and workstream owners to resolve dependencies and deliver commitments across functions.
Operational Excellence and Transformation
Lead redesign and simplification of priority processes, including cross-functional handoffs, controls, and ownership.
Deploy Lean, Kaizen, standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, and value stream improvements across selected Operations areas.
Partner with site and functional leaders to standardize practices while accommodating justified local needs and acquired businesses.
Systems and Automation
Set up and manage Operations Excellence portal for methodologies, documents, and training videos.
Partner with IT and process owners to define business requirements and integrate process redesign with enterprise systems, analytics, workflow automation, and appropriate AI-enabled solutions.
Drive adoption and effective use of Oracle and other enterprise platforms; reduce manual and spreadsheet-driven work where practical.
Establish consistent measures and reporting for the initiatives in the assigned portfolio.
Performance and Value Realization
Build baselines, benefit cases, milestones, and measurement plans with Finance and business owners.
Track Finance-validated impact on productivity, cost, margin, working capital, cash flow, and service; intervene when delivery or adoption falls short.
Develop a pipeline of improvement opportunities and ensure business owners sustain results after implementation.
Team and Change Leadership
Work individually while building a team. Manage and coach assigned program managers, improvement leads, and analysts; strengthen project management and problem-solving capability.
Build stakeholder alignment, communicate changes, and coordinate training and adoption plans.
Promote accountability, collaboration, respect for people, and data-driven decisions.
Qualifications
A minimum of 12 years of experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation or operational improvement programs in manufacturing, industrial technology, energy, or engineered products.
Demonstrated people leadership and ability to influence functional and site leaders without direct authority.
Practical knowledge of Lean, Kaizen, Six Sigma, A3, PDCA, or comparable methods.
Experience with enterprise systems implementation, process automation, performance metrics, and change management.
Strong financial acumen and experience quantifying and tracking operational benefits with Finance.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Finance, or a related discipline; Master’s degree preferred.
Success Measures First 6 to 12 Months
A governed portfolio of priority initiatives has clear owners, plans, milestones, risks, and a regular review cadence.
Initial initiatives deliver Finance-validated improvements in service, productivity, margin, or working capital.
Priority processes have documented standards and measurable adoption of Lean, Kaizen, systems, or automation improvements.
Functional leaders use consistent performance reporting to address delivery issues and sustain gains.
Working Relationships
Works closely with the Vice President and leaders across Operations, Engineering, Finance, IT, Sales, HR, business units, and sites to deliver the assigned transformation portfolio.

Plant Manager
M&M Manufacturing Company
Fort Worth, TX
M&M Manufacturing
As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.
Plant Manager
Who We Are
M&M Manufacturing
produces sheet metal ductwork, fittings, and accessories that support air distribution and ventilation in residential and commercial buildings. Join a team where you can help strengthen manufacturing operations, develop people, and deliver quality products that customers depend on.
As part of Marmon Holdings, Inc., a Berkshire Hathaway company, M&M Manufacturing combines the close-knit partnership of a smaller business with the resources and connectivity of a global organization. Here, people are encouraged to do work that matters, lead at every level, and win a better way through collaboration, continuous improvement, and meaningful results.
What You’ll Do
As the Plant Manager, you will
lead daily plant operations and put manufacturing strategies into action to support the company’s short- and long-term goals. Working with employees, sales teams, customers, and suppliers, you will build a safe, productive operation that delivers quality, customer satisfaction, and profitable growth.
Oversee production, maintenance, quality control, and inventory management to support efficient operations and dependable order fulfillment.
Establish operating priorities, streamline processes, and hold team members accountable for results.
Ensure compliance with environmental, health, safety, and regulatory requirements while building an active, positive safety culture.
Champion the M&M Manufacturing Lean Program and continuous improvement efforts to improve safety, productivity, efficiency, and operating income.
Monitor key performance indicators, analyze results, and lead corrective actions to meet plant targets.
Lead, coach, and develop plant employees through regular feedback, performance evaluations, and training, creating an inclusive environment that supports teamwork and professional growth.
Partner with the sales team to understand customer needs, fulfill orders accurately and on time, and identify opportunities for sales growth.
Build strong relationships with customers, suppliers, and other business partners.
Prepare and manage the plant budget, control expenses, and use financial analysis and reporting to guide decisions and improve profitability.
What You’ll Need
A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field; an advanced degree is preferred.
At least five years of experience in plant management or a similar role, preferably in an engineer-to-order or project-based manufacturing environment.
Proven experience managing plant operations, production processes, and maintenance.
Strong knowledge of safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
Working knowledge of Lean and/or Six Sigma methodologies, with the ability to drive continuous improvement.
Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, expense management, and financial analysis.
Proficiency with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and other relevant business software.
Effective leadership, team-building, coaching, communication, and presentation skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with ownership of plant performance and accountability for results.
The ability to build positive customer and stakeholder relationships, respond to internal and external customer needs, and remain open to new ideas and approaches.
What You’ll Gain
You will join a team where your contributions can make a visible difference. In addition, eligible employees may receive:
Competitive compensation aligned with the role, experience, and location.
Medical, dental, prescription, and vision coverage.
A 401(k) plan with company match.
Opportunities to learn, build new skills, and contribute to meaningful business results.
Following receipt of a conditional offer of employment, candidates will be required to complete additional job-related screening processes as permitted or required by applicable law.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and all applicants will be considered for employment without attention to their membership in any protected class. If you require any reasonable accommodation to complete your application or any part of the recruiting process, please email your request to careers@marmon.com, and please be sure to include the title and the location of the position for which you are applying.
